title: ML System Design — From Problem to Deployed Model

questions.question: A team reports an offline AUC of 0.91 for a churn model. What is missing before anyone can call the model useful?
options: The decision that uses each score and a baseline to compare against
A larger gradient-boosted model with more trees and a tuned learning rate
An AUC above 0.95, because production systems reject lower scores
A GPU server, because churn models need accelerators to serve traffic
questions.explanation: An offline metric alone says nothing about value. The design needs the action that each score starts and the strongest baseline that the model must beat.

questions.question: What is a guardrail metric?
options: A metric that only the security team is allowed to read
The metric with the largest value on the validation set
The offline metric that the training job minimizes on each batch
A metric that must not get worse when the new model launches
questions.explanation: Guardrails protect the parts of the system that the model is not trying to improve, such as cost, latency, and complaint rate.

questions.question: Scores must be at most 30 minutes old, and one full batch run takes one hour. What follows?
options: Batch inference still works if you run the job twice as often each day
Online inference cannot work, because it is slower than a key-value lookup read
Batch inference works if you add replicas to the key-value store
Batch inference cannot meet the limit, so the design needs online scoring
questions.explanation: A batch score is at least as old as one run. When the staleness limit is shorter than the job, no schedule can meet it.

questions.question: A churn model scores F1 0.56. The majority baseline scores 0.00, and a one-feature rule scores 0.46. What is the lift?
options: 0.51, the average gain over the two baselines in the comparison
0.10, measured against the rule, which is the strongest baseline
0.56, measured against the majority baseline, which scores zero
0.00, because lift is only defined against the current production system
questions.explanation: Lift is the gap to the strongest baseline. Comparing with the weakest baseline makes any model look good.

questions.question: A fraud model blocks risky payments, and the team retrains it each month on labeled payments. What problem does this create?
options: Blocked payments never get a fraud label, so the training data loses examples
The monthly retraining schedule makes the model overfit to the most recent month
Blocking payments raises the p99 latency of the model service above its budget
Labeled payments leak the label because the label is stored in the same table
questions.explanation: This is a feedback loop. The model's decisions remove outcomes from future training data, so keep a small random holdout that the model does not block.

questions.question: Which rollout stage lets a new model score live traffic while nobody uses its output?
options: Canary release
A/B test with a holdout
Shadow deployment
Full rollout with rollback
questions.explanation: In shadow mode, the system logs the new model's predictions and compares them with the current model. Users see only the current model's decisions.
